scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: HELP!! One workstation has completely FALLEN OFF the
network. It can't reach its gateway, can't reach its neighbours, can't reach
ANYTHING -- a total brick. Something around its socket into the network must
be wrong, but I don't know what. It worked on Friday! Could someone move it to
a working port and put it back on the network!! Work is piling up on that
desk!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
After exhaustive Layer 2 through Layer 3 investigation, the network is currently operating correctly. Every workstation in the topology — pc1 through pc14 and dc_pc5 — has a valid IP address, a correct default gateway, and full bidirectional reachability to its gateway and to every same-VLAN neighbour. Inter-VLAN routing between all five VLAN groups (VLAN 5, 6, 10, 20, 30) works end-to-end via OSPF, which has converged on both multilayer switches (mswitch0 and sshswitch).

The startup scripts for switch3 and sshswitch document two "translation bugs" that would have caused real workstation isolation had they been present in the running state: switch3 was originally missing the eth0.30 VLAN 30 trunk sub-interface, which would have left pc12, pc13, and pc14 in a completely isolated VLAN 30 bridge with no path to the mswitch0 SVI at 172.16.30.254; and sshswitch's eth0 was originally not wired to any bridge and lacked eth0.5/eth0.6 sub-interfaces, which would have cut off all VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 workstations on switch4 from their SVIs at 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254. Both fixes have been applied to the running kernel state and confirmed directly: switch3 eth0.30 is UP and forwarding in br_vlan30, and sshswitch eth0.5/eth0.6 are UP and forwarding in br_v5/br_v6. The helpdesk ticket almost certainly describes the condition that existed before these fixes were applied; the current lab state is healthy and no corrective action is required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup states broad reachability for pc1–pc14 but does not explicitly state that PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 and off‑subnet hosts with 0% loss.
